==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Xaml&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests.Windows/Extensions/XamlTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Xaml&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Windows;
using System.Windows.Controls;

// Verify.Xaml: Verifies a WPF window or element twice over: the serialized XAML tree and a rendered png.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Xaml
// Note: The tests have to run on an STA thread: [Apartment(ApartmentState.STA)] on the class for
// NUnit, [STAFact] for xUnit v3, [STATestClass] for MSTest, [STAThreadExecutor] for TUnit. Add the
// one for your framework to the generated class (plan U14).
// Note: Fixie and Expecto have no apartment mechanism, so no samples are generated for them.
// Note: Converters are registered for Window and FrameworkElement only, and each writes an xml
// target first and a png target second.
// Note: The XAML is re-emitted with one attribute per line, so a diff names the attribute that
// changed.
// Note: Attributes the capture path mutates, AllowsTransparency, ShowInTaskbar, WindowStyle,
// Opacity and Visibility, are stripped so the captured XAML matches the element as written.
// Note: The window is shown invisibly to force layout before it is rendered.
// Note: Rendering differs slightly between Windows versions; Verify.Phash or a custom comparer
// keeps the png target stable on a build agent.
// Note: The sample window is nested in the test class: the generated class library is not a WPF
// project.
// Note: WPF only: not UWP, WinUI, MAUI or Avalonia.
// Note: Windows only: the test project targets net10.0-windows and sets UseWPF.
public class XamlTests
{
    // Two snapshots come out of this: a .verified.xml holding the XAML tree, which reads well in
    // a diff, and a .verified.png of the rendered window, which catches what the tree cannot.
    // The class needs the STA attribute for the test framework in use; see the notes above.
    [Fact]
    public Task WindowUsage()
    {
        return Verify(new SampleWindow());
    }

    // A bare element has no window to be drawn in, so the converter hosts it in one. That means
    // a user control can be verified on its own, without the screen it normally lives on.
    [Fact]
    public Task FrameworkElement()
    {
        var panel = new StackPanel();
        panel.Children.Add(
            new TextBlock
            {
                Text = "Hello"
            });

        return Verify(panel);
    }

    // Stands in for a window of your own. Nested here rather than in the class library, which
    // is not a WPF project, so a Window cannot live there.
    class SampleWindow :
        Window
    {
        public SampleWindow()
        {
            Title = "Sample";
            Width = 200;
            Height = 100;
            Content = new TextBlock
            {
                Text = "Hello"
            };
        }
    }
}

==== interactions

Info avalonia-mvvm: Many Avalonia and WPF projects use CommunityToolkit.Mvvm. Verify.CommunityToolkit.Mvvm snapshots its observable properties and commands readably, rather than as generated members.
